ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The plot shows an impulse train on the time axis. The visible impulses occur in repeated clusters: one cluster is centered at t = -6 with smaller impulses at t = -7 and t = -5, another is centered at t = 0 with smaller impulses at t = -1 and t = 1, and another is centered at t = 6 with smaller impulses at t = 5 and t = 7. In each cluster, the center impulse is taller than the adjacent side impulses, and the relative pattern of heights is the same from cluster to cluster. Reasoning: Comparing the cluster centered at t = 0 with the clusters centered at t = -6 and t = 6, a horizontal shift of 6 maps the impulse at -1 to 5, the impulse at 0 to 6, and the impulse at 1 to 7, preserving the same relative heights. Similarly, shifting by 6 maps the cluster {-7, -6, -5} to {-1, 0, 1}. Therefore T = 6 is a period. A smaller positive shift would not map each tall center impulse to another equal tall center impulse and would mismatch the smaller side impulses, so no smaller positive period works. Thus the fundamental period is T0 = 6.

Compare the cluster centered at t=0 with the clusters centered at t=-6 and t=6. A horizontal shift of 6 maps the impulse at -1 to 5, 0 to 6, and 1 to 7, preserving the relative heights; similarly it maps {-7,-6,-5} to {-1,0,1}. Then rule out any smaller positive shift by noting that it would move a tall center impulse to a location where no equal tall impulse exists or would mismatch the smaller side impulses. Therefore the fundamental period is T0=6.

method.method_draft: Translate the plotted signal into an impulse-comb description, e.g. \tilde{x}(t)=\sum_k[\delta(t-6k)+\tfrac12\delta(t-(6k-1))+\tfrac12\delta(t-(6k+1))], up to the amplitudes read from the figure. Each of the three shifted impulse combs repeats every 6 units, so the whole signal has period 6. Test possible smaller periods by observing that a smaller shift would have to map the amplitude-1 impulses at multiples of 6 onto other amplitude-1 impulses; the nearest such impulses are 6 units apart, so no smaller positive period works. Hence T0=6.
